    "title": "Build-time codegen scripts: idempotent writes and temp-dir test isolation are mandatory design constraints",
    "content": "When writing a build-time script that generates a derivative file from a source-of-truth (e.g. a JSON registry → a typed TypeScript wrapper), two design constraints are non-negotiable: (1) **Idempotent write** — compare the generated content against the current file on disk before writing; skip the write if they are identical. (2) **Temp-dir test isolation** — test cases that verify the codegen produces or mutates an output file must operate against a controlled temporary directory that mirrors only the needed file structure, never against the live project root. A test that mutates the real output file cannot auto-revert in a test harness, leaving the repository in a dirty state after test runs. 1	# Model Registry
     2	
     3	The `model-registry/` directory holds the file-based model configuration for the persona system. It contains three files with distinct lifecycles:
     4	
     5	| File | Tracked in Git | Purpose |
     6	|---|---|---|
     7	| `default.json` | ✅ Yes | Shipped seed models. Copied into `local.json` on first access. |
     8	| `local.json` | ❌ No (gitignored) | Working copy of the model list. Single source of truth at runtime. |
     9	| `assignments.json` | ❌ No (gitignored) | Per-persona model assignments and the global default model selection. |
    10	
    11	## How `default.json` and `local.json` Relate
    12	
    13	`default.json` is a **seed file**, not a runtime layer. It exists solely so new installations start with a sensible set of models. At runtime:
    14	
    15	1. On first access, `local.json` is auto-initialized by copying all entries from `default.json`.
    16	2. The GUI's **Load Defaults** button re-runs this merge on demand — new default entries (identified by `id`) are added to `local.json`; entries that already exist are left unchanged.
    17	3. Once copied into `local.json`, entries are fully editable and deletable like any user-registered model.
    18	
    19	There is no concept of "built-in" vs. "custom" at runtime — `local.json` is the single source of truth for the model list. `default.json` is never read during normal operation.
    20	
    21	## Entry Schema
    22	
    23	Each entry in `default.json` (and `local.json`) is a JSON object with exactly four fields:
    24	
    25	| Field | Type | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|
    27	| `id` | UUID string | Stable primary key. Never changes after creation — even if `name` or `slug` is edited. |
    28	| `name` | string | Human-readable display name (shown in the GUI). |
    29	| `slug` | string | URL-safe identifier used internally for model resolution. |
    30	| `cc_model` | string | Claude Code model value. See [cc_model values](#cc_model-values) below. |
    31	
    32	### `cc_model` Values
    33	
    34	- **`"inherit"`** — Claude Code defers to the user's configured model. Use this for Anthropic models, where Claude Code's built-in `inherit` behaviour is appropriate.
    35	- **Explicit model name** (e.g., `"gemini-3-5-flash"`) — Use this for non-Anthropic models that Claude Code cannot resolve via `inherit`.
    36	
    37	## Formatting Convention
    38	
    39	Entries in `default.json` use **single-line inline JSON**, one object per line, with fields in the order `id`, `name`, `slug`, `cc_model`. This keeps diffs minimal (one line changed per entry) and makes the file easy to scan:
    40	
    41	```json
    42	[
    43	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "name": "Inherit / Auto", "slug": "inherit", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    44	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001", "name": "Claude Opus 4.6", "slug": "claude-opus-4-6", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    45	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002", "name": "Claude Sonnet 4.6", "slug": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    46	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003", "name": "Gemini 3.5 Flash", "slug": "gemini-3-5-flash", "cc_model": "gemini-3-5-flash" }
    47	]
    48	```
    49	
    50	Maintain this convention when adding new default entries so that `git diff` output remains readable.
    51	
    52	## Deterministic Zero-Namespace UUIDs
    53	
    54	Default entries use **deterministic zero-namespace UUIDs** — sequential values starting at `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`. This is intentional:
    55	
    56	- **Stable across installations** — the same UUID always refers to the same default model, regardless of when or where the workspace was cloned.
    57	- **Safe merge-by-ID in `loadDefaults()`** — when loading defaults into `local.json`, the merge logic matches entries by `id`. Deterministic UUIDs guarantee that the "Inherit / Auto" entry (id `000...000`) or "Claude Sonnet 4.6" (id `000...002`) can never accidentally collide with a user-generated entry (which uses randomly-generated UUIDs).
    58	
    59	When adding a new default model to `default.json`, assign the next sequential zero-namespace UUID (e.g., `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000004`).
    60	
    61	## The "Inherit / Auto" Sentinel
    62	
    63	The first entry — slug `inherit`, id `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` — is a **sentinel value**. When a persona is assigned this model:
    64	
    65	- **VS Code output:** The `model` frontmatter field is omitted entirely (the user's model picker selection takes effect).
    66	- **Claude Code output:** `model: 'inherit'` is set in frontmatter (Claude Code defers to the user's configured model).
    67	- **Orchestrator:** Skips the assignment and falls back to YAML-based resolution.
    68	
    69	Consumers identify the sentinel by checking `slug === 'inherit'` on the resolved slug — no special-case structure is needed in assignment storage.
    70	
    71	## Adding a New Default Model
    72	
    73	1. Open `default.json`.
    74	2. Append a new entry at the end of the array using the next sequential zero-namespace UUID.
    75	3. Set `cc_model` to `"inherit"` for Anthropic models, or to the explicit model name for non-Anthropic models.
    76	4. Follow the single-line inline JSON formatting convention.
    77	5. The new entry will be merged into existing `local.json` files the next time **Load Defaults** is triggered from the GUI.
    78	
    79	## Further Reading
    80	
    81	- [Personas Build System](../README.md) — Overview of the template engine and suite structure
    82	- [Plan: Model Settings](../../docs/agents/plans/2026-07-21-model-settings/plan.md) — Architecture decisions and rationale for the model registry design
